# Figure captions

*Auto-generated by `scripts/generate_paper_assets.py` from saved results. Every asset has its underlying data next to it (CSV/JSON).*

- **`results/figures/diagrams/fig01_system_architecture`** — SACENet system overview. Solid components were trained and evaluated on MC-Hinglish1.0. The dashed early-warning path was evaluated only on the English CONDA proxy dataset.
- **`results/figures/diagrams/fig02_data_pipeline`** — Dataset acquisition and preprocessing pipeline (scripts/download_datasets.py → verify_datasets.py → prepare_data.py).
- **`results/figures/diagrams/fig03_model_architecture`** — Classifier architecture shared by MuRIL, XLM-R and HingRoBERTa runs. The sarcasm head exists only in the multitask variants; CE_w is class-weighted cross-entropy.
- **`results/figures/diagrams/fig04_sarcasm_components`** — Two ways of injecting sarcasm knowledge learned from the human-annotated Swami et al. (2018) corpus. (a) multitask learning with a shuffled-label control; (b) feature fusion with a separately trained, frozen sarcasm model (its P(sarcastic) and pooled embedding).
- **`results/figures/diagrams/fig05_early_detection_workflow`** — Causal early-warning procedure. It was evaluated only on CONDA (English in-game chat) as a proxy, because no openly available Hinglish conversation dataset has turn-level cyberbullying labels.
- **`results/figures/diagrams/fig06_methodology`** — Experimental methodology.
- **`results/figures/data/fig07_dataset_distributions`** — Class distributions of the datasets after splitting. MC-Hinglish validation is carved from the official training split; the official test split is unchanged.
- **`results/figures/data/fig08_language_distribution`** — Language composition. Left: gold token-level language tags released with the Swami et al. corpus. Right: share of English function words (scikit-learn English stop-word list) per MC-Hinglish test comment. This is a heuristic proxy for English content, since MC-Hinglish has no language tags. All MC-Hinglish texts are in Roman script.
- **`results/figures/training/fig09_training_curves_mc7`** — Training and validation loss and validation macro-F1 per epoch on MC7 (seed 13). The checkpoint with the highest validation macro-F1 is evaluated on test.
- **`results/figures/evaluation/fig11_confusion_mc7`** — Confusion matrices on the official MC-Hinglish1.0 test set (counts; shading = row-normalised recall).
- **`results/figures/evaluation/fig12_roc_pr`** — ROC and precision–recall curves of seed-ensembled probabilities on the binary tasks. Dotted lines: chance (ROC) and positive-class prevalence (PR). The 7-class task uses macro one-vs-rest AUC, reported in Table 3.
- **`results/figures/comparison/fig14_model_comparison_mc7`** — Seven-way macro-F1 on the official test set and on its subset without near-duplicates of training items. Transformers: mean ± s.d. over 3 seeds. Baselines are deterministic (single run). The x-axis does not start at 0.
- **`results/figures/ablation/fig15_ablation_sarcasm`** — Ablation of the sarcasm components on MC7 (MuRIL). Controls: MTL with permuted sarcasm labels, and fusion with features from a sarcasm model trained on permuted labels. A gain over the matching control would be attributable to sarcasm knowledge; none is observed.
- **`results/figures/explainability/fig16_shap_token_attributions`** — Word-level SHAP attributions (subword values summed) for selected MC7 test comments explained with respect to the predicted class. Attributions describe the model's sensitivity, not the author's intent. Texts are shown as distributed (CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0); offensive content is not censored, for scientific transparency.
- **`results/figures/explainability/fig16b_shap_faithfulness`** — Faithfulness check on 100 random MC7 test comments: drop in the predicted-class probability after deleting the k words with the highest SHAP value vs. k random words (10 draws).
- **`results/figures/error_analysis/fig17_error_slices`** — Accuracy on test slices. Slices are defined by heuristics (profanity lexicon, English function-word share, out-of-vocabulary rate relative to training text) or by the sarcasm model's prediction. None is a gold annotation; small slices have wide uncertainty.
- **`results/figures/runtime/fig18_runtime_size`** — Inference latency (median of repeated single-comment predictions) and serialized model size, measured on an Apple M1 Pro (16 GB).
- **`results/figures/calibration/fig19_calibration_mc7`** — Reliability diagram on the MC7 test set before and after temperature scaling (T fitted on validation).
- **`results/figures/early_detection/fig20_early_detection_proxy`** — Early-warning proxy study on CONDA test conversations (English game chat; not cyberbullying, not Hinglish). Threshold chosen on validation conversations. A negative delay means the alarm fired on a non-toxic turn before the first toxic turn.
